To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cetuximab dosing Q2W versus weekly was not associated with inferior OS in patients with mCRC.
cetuximab Q2W was noninferior to cetuximab once weekly for overall survival in patients with metastatic colorectal carcinoma.
cetuximab dosed every 2  weeks was not inferior to once weekly for OS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparative effectiveness of Q2W versus once weekly cetuximab.
the comparative effectiveness of cetuximabs administered Q2W and every week in the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancers.
the noninferior efficacy of cetuximabb administered every two weeks (Q2W), versus once weekly (q1W).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cetuximab Q2W is noninferior to cetuximab Q1W for OS, and that Q2W dosing may be an option for patients who cannot tolerate the Q1W dosing.
Q2W cetuximab was noninferior to Q1W cetuximabb for OS, but with the caveat that the noninferior margin was 1.3, which is larger than that used in clinical studies.
the Q2W regimen of cetuximabb was noninferior to the Q1W regimen with regard to OS in patients with mCRC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Q2W regimen was noninferior to the standard Q1W regimen in terms of OS and safety in a US-insurance database, and the Q2W schedule could be considered as a viable option for patients who cannot afford or tolerate cetuximab.
Q2W cetuximab is noninferior to Q1W cetuximah for OS in mCRC.
cetuximab is a safe and effective treatment for mCRC, regardless of the frequency of administration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Q2W administration of cetuximabb may offer a more convenient and cost-effective alternative for patients with mCRC.
the efficacy of cetuximabb is maintained when it is administered Q2W.
Q2W administration may be a reasonable option in the management of patients with mCRC.
